summary: Provisioner API rate-limit causes runner provisioning backlog during concurrent credential rewrap
description:
Issue summary:
During a planned credential rewrap window for Vault in us-west1, our runner provisioner started hitting upstream cloud API rate-limits which produced a sustained provisioning backlog. This caused a ~45m CI queue spike in us-west1 and degraded release throughput for teams using nightly and canary pipelines.

Impact:
- CI job queue backlog for ephemerally-provisioned runners in us-west1 between 2026-03-10T03:15 and 2026-03-10T04:00.
- Several release canaries timed out (timeout threshold 20m) and were rerun, delaying rollouts.
- No customer-facing outage; internal release velocity impaired.

Environment:
- prod cluster: k8s-prod-us-west1 (runner-provisioner v2.8.1)
- Vault cluster: vault-us-west1 (transit rewrap wave B)
- Provisioner uses cloud provider API (compute) to create ephemeral VMs and attach service account keys; these calls are proxied through the provisioner control-plane.

Steps to reproduce (observed):
1) Start bulk vault key rewrap job for transit key (wave B) which triggered re-issuance of short-lived credentials for the provisioner service-account.
2) Provisioner attempted to refresh credentials mid-provision for ~120 concurrent runner requests (autoscaling burst during nightly convergence).
3) Provisioner retried cloud API create-instance calls after transient auth failures; retries were aggressive (exponential backoff with short cap) and overlapped, exceeding provider rate-limits.
4) Cloud API returned 429s and 503s; provisioner entered a retry loop, inflating queued work and preventing new jobs from being scheduled to other pools.

Observed behavior:
- Provisioner metrics: create_instance_errors spiked to 18/min, retry_count doubled, queue_depth increased to 320.
- Runner controller recorded pod pending times > 10 minutes; some pods evicted mid-provision.
- Vault logs show credential re-issuance for provisioner principal at 2026-03-10T03:12Z (wave B).

Expected behavior:
- Provisioner should gracefully fallback to cached service-account token until rewrap completes and should not trigger concurrent aggressive retries that cause upstream rate-limits.
- Bulk rewrap should include a coordination step with provisioner to stagger refreshes or use rolling rebind to avoid synchronized credential churn.

Investigation notes:
- Hypothesis: credential rewrap caused simultaneous token expiry/refresh across provisioner workers, creating a thundering herd when each worker attempted cloud API calls with a short window of renewed tokens.
- We observed that the provisioner does an immediate KMS decryption + SA key re-fetch on first request after rewrap; under load, many workers hit that path concurrently.
- Retry policy in provisioner was configured with max_attempts=8 and initial_backoff=200ms. With hundreds of parallel requests this escalated quickly.
- Cloud provider rate-limits were per-project and the transient 429s caused cascading retries from other services (not just provisioner).
- No rollback of the rewrap was possible mid-wave; however, rewrap was completed ~03:30 and provisioning recovered after tokens stabilized.

Temporary mitigation applied:
- At 03:22 SRE throttled incoming CI requests from the orchestrator for non-critical pipelines and enabled a soft cap on concurrent ephemeral runner creation for us-west1 to 30 concurrent new instances. This reduced pressure and allowed rewrap to complete.
- Adjusted provisioner retry backoff to be more conservative (initial_backoff=1s, max_attempts=5) to limit cascade while we validated token stability. Change rolled as emergency config patch across provisioner replicas.

Root cause (working hypothesis):
- Simultaneous credential rewrap + aggressive provisioner retry policy + autoscaling burst produced upstream provider rate-limit exhaustion which backfed into provisioner queue growth.

Resolution plan / next steps (action items):
- Short term (P0/P1):
  - Ship a provisioner patch to add jittered credential refresh and stronger single-flight token refresh across worker threads (owner: Diego Moreno, due: 2026-03-12).
  - Make retry policy conservative by default for cloud create calls (owner: Provisioner team, due: 2026-03-12).
  - Add a guard in release orchestration to limit parallel ephemeral-runner provisioning per region during scheduled key rewrap windows (owner: Release Eng, due: 2026-03-15).
- Medium term:
  - Coordinate with Vault team to implement a rewrap stagger plan (waves with token-stabilization window) and publish rewrap-calendar to support teams (owner: Security/Secrets, due: 2026-04-01).
  - Add quota-aware provisioning fallback: if upstream 429 observed, move requests to standby dedicated pools or queue with exponential backoff and notify SRE (owner: Provisioner, due: 2026-04-08).
  - Postmortem and retrospective runbook update to include checks before initiating waves that affect service accounts used by high-throughput components.

Follow-ups / Monitoring:
- New metrics to add: single_flight_token_refresh_rate, token_refresh_failure_rate, provisioner_concurrent_refresh_count. (owner: Observability, due: 2026-03-19).
- Alerting: add alert for create_instance_errors > 5/min sustained for 5m and queue_depth > 200.

Notes and links:
- Cloud provider rate-limit incident doc: https://cloud.example.com/limits/INC-2026-03
- Vault rewrap runbook: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/SEC/Vault+Rewrap+Runbook
- Provisioner config and recent change: https://github.com/redwood/provisioner/commit/4a9d2f2
